review_items.rationale: Reviewed artifact 6f58603f998044dfbe39d24fcbff47d0 version 1, its fixed harness/plan, claim C_read_joint_eligibility version 1, binding BIND_read_joint_consumer version 1, execution e5a5dd0477a44775af322e051af102a8 and raw CA_EVENT observations. The accepted local duty follows safe-read quorum communication and JointConfig requiring both majorities; it is not a proof of full linearizability. The single unique request eliminates the alternative mechanism where a later read context releases earlier requests. RawNode is called sequentially through actual Bootstrap, Campaign, ReadIndex and ProposeConfChange, with committed configuration entries applied through ApplyConfChange. No protocol state is injected. The async worker adapter preserves per-target FIFO and performs MemoryStorage writes before returning attached responses; physical durability remains modeled and no crash occurs. Four genuine heartbeat responses for the same request and term 2 are produced before the configuration change, retained unchanged, and released after an actual committed/applied explicit-joint change at index 7. The joint_prefix observation confirms incoming [1,4,5], outgoing [1,2,3,4,5], term 2, applied 7 and pre_joint_outputs=0. Thus cumulative output measurements cannot be confused with a release under the old configuration in this execution. The independent ledger counts local dispatch as self participation and remote senders only at their actual Step delivery, never consulting readOnly.acks. Since the leader remains voter 1 in term 2 and the measured voter sets do not change again, the ledger correctly represents the selected acknowledgment eligibility question. Its thresholds are 2 incoming and 3 outgoing, taken from the fixed sets rather than implementation quorum functions. The first three checkpoints observed incoming/outgoing counts (1,1), (1,2), (1,3) with zero ReadStates. After actual reply 4, the read_output event itself records counts (2,4), context unique-read-joint-1 and index 6; the subsequent checkpoint records one output. Reply 5 leaves one output with counts (3,5). This emission-time diagnostic confirms that the cumulative checkpoint comparison did not hide an earlier unqualified release. The read index 6 predates the configuration at index 7, as expected from the stored original request index; the oracle does not incorrectly demand a latest-index value. All five admissions have unique request/phase correlations, precede their results, and depend on reached joint configuration rather than release success. Parser errors and missing results are absent; result indices 113/116/119/123/126 correlate with admissions 112/114/117/120/124. The fixed scheduler finishes independently of the predicate, and read_history_finished records one output and zero held replies. The one-way implication is satisfied at the measured checkpoints, with an actual qualified-output control. No correspondence issue was found within the declared scope.
limitations: This is a local ReadState eligibility result, not an observed client read or a complete linearizability argument.

Only one fresh context, one explicit voter reduction and one unchanged leader term were executed; request batching, retries, learner promotion and later role/configuration transitions remain untested here.

The monitor measures five fixed checkpoints. The actual emission event confirms correct qualification in this execution, without establishing exhaustive intermediate-state coverage for other histories.
MemoryStorage and deterministic worker/transport queues are documented substitutions; crash durability and failure-recovery endpoints are excluded.
Pending output when a majority is missing is permitted; no liveness bound or universal sufficiency theorem follows from the completing control.
